drugRefs.dose: Ceftriaxone 2 g IV q24h + Metronidazole 500-750 mg IV/PO q8h
drugRefs.duration: 2-4 weeks depending on response and whether drainage performed
drugRefs.why: This combination covers the most likely pyogenic pathogens (Klebsiella, E. coli, anaerobes) while metronidazole simultaneously provides empiric amebic coverage, addressing both major causes pending specific identification.

drugRefs.coverage: Broader single-agent alternative if biliary source or polymicrobial infection is more strongly suspected; add metronidazole/amebic-specific therapy separately if amebic etiology cannot be excluded.

coverageMatrix.completeness: Combination therapy covers both leading pyogenic organisms and amebic disease pending specific diagnosis.
gaps: Definitive distinction between pyogenic and amebic abscess (and targeted single-agent therapy) requires aspirate analysis or serology.

stewardship.deescalation: If aspirate/serology confirms isolated amebic abscess, discontinue antibacterial agents and continue metronidazole alone (followed by a luminal agent to clear colonic cysts). If purely pyogenic with a known organism, narrow to the single most targeted antibacterial agent.

drugs.dose: Ceftriaxone 2 g IV q24h + Metronidazole 500-750 mg IV/PO q8h
drugs.duration: 2-4 weeks depending on response and whether drainage performed
drugs.why: This combination covers the most likely pyogenic pathogens (Klebsiella, E. coli, anaerobes) while metronidazole simultaneously provides empiric amebic coverage, addressing both major causes pending specific identification.

drugs.coverage: Broader single-agent alternative if biliary source or polymicrobial infection is more strongly suspected; add metronidazole/amebic-specific therapy separately if amebic etiology cannot be excluded.

framework: Image-guided aspiration or drainage of abscesses >5cm (or any size with risk of rupture) is an important adjunct to antibiotics, not a replacement — pursue source control in parallel.

Once amebic serology/aspirate confirms a single diagnosis, narrow therapy accordingly (discontinue antibacterial agents if purely amebic; discontinue metronidazole's amebic-dose course if purely pyogenic and anaerobic coverage isn't separately needed).
In diabetic patients with Klebsiella liver abscess, screen for endophthalmitis (a recognized association), since this changes management and prognosis.
